## Context / Problem
`rebar store fsck` parses its argv by hand (`fsck_cli`, `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py`). It picks out the flags it knows (`--repair`, `--dry-run`, `--repair-snapshots`, `--include-archived`, `--only`, `--limit`, the output flags) and drops everything else, so an unknown or misspelled flag exits 0 with no message.

Observed on origin/main `aa1681bb531` in a scratch store (2026-11-13):
- `rebar store fsck --bogus` exits 0 and runs a normal check.
- `rebar store fsck --limit` (no value) exits 0; the bare flag is dropped.
- `rebar store fsck --repair --dryrun` (typo for `--dry-run`) runs the REAL repair: output `ensures: swept 10 unit(s); 0 changed, 0 failed`, where `--repair --dry-run` only reports. A typo turns a preview into a mutation of the store.

`rebar store compact` already rejects unknown options (`Error: unknown option '--threshold'`, exit 1), so fsck is the odd one out.

## Approach
In `fsck_cli`, after the known flags are taken out and `parse_output` runs, reject any leftover argument: write `Error: unknown option '<arg>'` plus the usage line to stderr and return 2, before any store access or repair. Reject a bare `--limit` the same way `--only` already is (`Error: --limit requires a value`, exit 2). No new flag, config key or env var.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar store fsck --bogus` exits 2 and stderr names `--bogus`.
- [x] `rebar store fsck --repair --dryrun` exits 2 and makes no change to the store (no ensure sweep, no commit).
- [x] `rebar store fsck --limit` exits 2 with `--limit requires a value`.
- [x] Every documented spelling still works: `--only stale-channel --repair`, `--only=stale-channel --repair`, `--limit 1`, `--limit=1`, `--include-archived`, `--repair-snapshots`, `--dry-run`, and the output flags; proved by `pytest tests/unit/test_fsck_only_flag.py`.

## Testing
Add RED tests to `tests/unit/test_fsck_only_flag.py` for the 3 rejected forms (exit 2, message, and for the typo case no repair call), then make them pass. Run `pytest tests/unit/test_fsck_only_flag.py` and `make verify`.
